text:
ok cool now ive been doing some forward thinking and while we arnt there yet this is something we can think about i like the idea of im thinking im going to do my mission / story / objective system authoring (like dialog, and title, and overview) as a markdown file that can parse into json and append all the game data to it when it comes to rigging so t hat i can collectively over time even before any of that gets set up be writing up all the ideas i do have into actual artifacts to be used and for future case is a great way to treat how they can be made by anyone via markdown as t he stepping stone. thinking it might be more up my own alley to actually use something like a <block> format that the authoring by hand and in editor both append to, and overtime this could technically teach someone how to do it all by hand
<npc>
<name>Claude</name>
<bio>A Smart Fella</bio>
<ref>myfriendclaude</ref>
<model>@[link]</model>
.
.
.
</npc>

and then in a mission file do 

<mission>
<name>Something Clever</name>
<desc>Learn something about a friend.</desc>
<offered_by>@[myfriendclaude]</offered_by> #mainnpc
<dialog>
<mainnpc>Hello friend</mainnpc>
.
.
.
.

as a quick and dirty idea to spit ball for you
resolution: Design answer, no code: endorsed the markdown-with-block mission/NPC authoring format as the human text SOURCE tier the rulings already reserved — V22 rules missions as rows over a CLOSED schema (LLM dailies write the same rows, so hand/editor/LLM become three producers of one compile) and V29 rules text keyvalue entities as platform-opaque. Gave format guardrails: blocks stay declarative (branching = objective graph refs, never inline conditionals per GUIDING_LIGHT), stable ref vs mutable display name (the req_2735 id-vs-name lesson), effects as closed-schema world_deltas, prose between blocks = designer notes the parser ignores. Encouraged starting to write artifacts NOW; saved memory project_mission_block_authoring so the eventual parser/compile slice inherits the intent.
